newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Secondary shares show only spark on Russian market.
newsitem.headline: Secondary shares show only spark on Russian market.

text.p: Russian shares drifted on Monday though a few second-tier shares firmed for the day and traders said the market, overheated by January's bull run, would probably stay calm for the near term.

Chelyabenergo led the market, followed by other second tier shares, and climbed to $0.38 from $0.32, which one trader attributed to a lack of liquidity and better than expected results released last week.
The Russian Trading System 24-share index edged up 0.76 percent to 276.67 on a slim $17.4 million volume for the entire market but traders said that second-tier shares saw some Western demand.
Krasnoyarskenergo firmed to $0.38 from $0.36 and a number of shares traded up on small volumes. Traders said there was interest in Gazprom, which ticked up to $0.471 from $0.470.

Mosenergo shrugged off news it expected only a modest decline in profits this year because it was freezing power charges. The price was hit last week on Russian press reports of a substantial drop in profits this year. It finished at $1.40 after $1.46 on Friday.
Olma senior trader Oleg Dobritsky said that there had been relatively strong demand on the RTS-2 system of second and third tier shares.
ING Barings chief equities trader Peter Kizenko estimated the market would stay within an eight to 10 percent range until the end of February before a new flow of funds revitalised the market.

"The appetite for the blue chips has been satiated, probably for the next couple of weeks," he said. "You might see some locals get impatient, and cause the next downward move before the next flow comes in."
Operators said investors were still calculating where to move next but generally expect the rally to continue.
